nodes.title: Carbohydrates Classification & Monosaccharides
points: Carbohydrates: Optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or polyhydroxy ketones, or compounds that produce them on hydrolysis. General formula C_x(H₂O)_y.

Classification: Monosaccharides (cannot be hydrolyzed further: glucose, fructose, ribose); Oligosaccharides (yield 2 to 10 monosaccharides: disaccharides like sucrose, maltose, lactose); Polysaccharides (yield large number of monosaccharides: starch, cellulose, glycogen).

Reducing vs Non-reducing sugars: Reducing sugars contain free or potentially free aldehydic/ketonic carbonyl group and reduce Tollens' and Fehling's reagents (all monosaccharides, maltose, lactose). Non-reducing sugar: glycosidic linkage involves both anomeric carbons (sucrose).
Aldohexose (Glucose) vs Ketohexose (Fructose).

formulas.label: General carbohydrate empirical formula
formulas.expr: C_x(H₂O)_y (e.g. Glucose: C₆H₁₂O₆ where x=6, y=6)

formulas.label: Disaccharide hydrolysis general equation
formulas.expr: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O (H⁺ or enzyme) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + C₆H₁₂O₆

nodes.title: D-Glucose: Open Chain Structure & Proof Reactions
points: Molecular formula: C₆H₁₂O₆.
1. Straight chain of 6 carbons: Prolonged heating with HI + red P → n-hexane.
2. Presence of carbonyl group: Reacts with hydroxylamine (NH₂OH) → monoxime; Reacts with HCN → cyanohydrin.
3. Carbonyl is an aldehyde: Mild oxidation with Bromine water (Br₂/H₂O) → Gluconic acid (C₆H₁₂O₇, mono-carboxylic acid).
4. Presence of 5 −OH groups: Acetylation with acetic anhydride (Ac₂O) → Glucose pentaacetate (stable, indicating 5 −OH groups on 5 different carbons).
5. Presence of 1° alcohol group: Strong oxidation with dilute HNO₃ → Saccharic acid / Glucaric acid (HOOC−(CHOH)₄−COOH, dicarboxylic acid).
D-Configuration: OH on the lowest asymmetric carbon (C-5) is on the right side in Fischer projection. D-(+)-glucose is dextrorotatory.

nodes.title: Cyclic Structure of Glucose & Mutarotation
points: Limitations of open chain: Does not give 2,4-DNP test or Schiff's test; does not form hydrogen sulfite addition compound with NaHSO₃; Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine (proves absent free −CHO).
Cyclic hemiacetal formation: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of C-5 −OH to C-1 −CHO group forming a 6-membered pyranose ring (glucopyranose).
Anomers: Diastereomers differing only in configuration at C-1 (anomeric carbon):
- α-D-(+)-glucopyranose: C-1 −OH is on right in Fischer (down in Haworth), melting point 419 K, specific rotation +112°.
- β-D-(+)-glucopyranose: C-1 −OH is on left in Fischer (up in Haworth), melting point 423 K, specific rotation +19°.
Mutarotation: Spontaneous change in specific optical rotation of an optically active solution over time until an equilibrium value is reached (+52.7° at equilibrium containing 36% α and 64% β).

formulas.label: Glucopyranose ring structure
formulas.expr: Six-membered pyranose ring formed by hemiacetal linkage between C-1 and C-5 oxygen

nodes.title: Disaccharides: Sucrose, Maltose, Lactose & Invert Sugar
points: Glycosidic linkage: Oxide / ether linkage (−O−) formed between two monosaccharide units by loss of a water molecule.
1. Sucrose (Cane Sugar): Non-reducing sugar; composed of α-D-glucopyranose (C-1) and β-D-fructofuranose (C-2) joined by C1-C2 glycosidic linkage. Both reducing groups are tied up!

Invert Sugar: Sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°); on acid hydrolysis gives equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose (+52.7°) and D-(−)-fructose (−92.4°). Since levorotation of fructose is greater than dextrorotation of glucose, the resulting mixture is levorotatory (−19.8°). This sign inversion from (+) to (−) is called Inversion of Cane Sugar!
2. Maltose: Reducing sugar; composed of two α-D-glucose units joined by α-1,4-glycosidic linkage. Free C-1 anomeric carbon at second ring.
3. Lactose (Milk Sugar): Reducing sugar; composed of β-D-galactose (C-1) and β-D-glucose (C-4) joined by β-1,4-glycosidic linkage.

nodes.title: Polysaccharides: Starch, Cellulose & Glycogen
points: 1. Starch (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ: Main storage polysaccharide of plants. Polymer of α-D-glucose. Consists of two components:
- Amylose (15-20%): Water soluble, linear unbranched chain of α-D-glucose linked by α-1,4-glycosidic bonds (200-1000 units); gives blue color with iodine.
- Amylopectin (80-85%): Water insoluble, branched chain. Main chain α-1,4-glycosidic bonds; branching occurs via α-1,6-glycosidic bonds every 20-25 units; gives reddish-purple color with iodine.
2. Cellulose: Structural component of plant cell walls. Linear, unbranched polymer of β-D-glucose linked by β-1,4-glycosidic bonds. Humans cannot digest cellulose because they lack cellulase enzyme.
3. Glycogen (Animal Starch): Storage polysaccharide in animal liver and muscles. Structurally similar to amylopectin but much more highly branched (branching every 8-12 units).

formulas.label: Starch component percentages
formulas.expr: Amylose: 15-20% (water-soluble, linear α-1,4) | Amylopectin: 80-85% (insoluble, branched α-1,4 & α-1,6)

formulas.label: Cellulose glycosidic linkage
formulas.expr: Linear polymer of β-D-glucose linked by β-1,4-glycosidic bonds

nodes.title: Amino Acids: Classification, Zwitterion & Isoelectric Point
points: Structure: Contain amino group (−NH₂) and carboxyl group (−COOH) on α-carbon: R−CH(NH₂)−COOH.
Classification by nature: Neutral (equal NH₂ and COOH, e.g. glycine, alanine); Acidic (excess COOH, e.g. aspartic acid, glutamic acid); Basic (excess NH₂, e.g. lysine, arginine, histidine).
Essential vs Non-essential: Essential (cannot be synthesized by body, must be in diet: Val, Leu, Ile, Lys, Met, Phe, Thr, Trp); Non-essential (synthesized by body: Gly, Ala, etc.).
Optical activity: All naturally occurring amino acids are optically active and have L-configuration, EXCEPT Glycine (H₂N−CH₂−COOH is achiral).
Zwitterion (Dipolar ion): In aqueous solution, acidic −COOH loses a proton to basic −NH₂: R−CH(⁺NH₃)−COO⁻. Has high melting point, water soluble, amphoteric.
Isoelectric Point (pI): The specific pH at which an amino acid exists predominantly as neutral dipolar zwitterion and carries no net electrical charge; does not migrate in an electric field.

formulas.label: Isoelectric point (pI) calculation for neutral amino acid
Glycine achirality note
formulas.expr: H₂N-CH₂-COOH (two -H atoms on α-carbon; only achiral natural amino acid)

nodes.title: Proteins: Peptide Linkage, Structural Levels & Denaturation
points: Peptide Linkage (amide bond −CO−NH−): Formed between −COOH of one amino acid and −NH₂ of another with elimination of H₂O.

Structural levels of proteins: 1) Primary (1°): Linear sequence of amino acids linked by peptide bonds; 2) Secondary (2°): Regular folding of polypeptide backbone stabilized by hydrogen bonding between >C=O and −NH− (α-Helix right-handed spiral; β-Pleated Sheet zigzag sheets); 3) Tertiary (3°): Overall 3D folding into globular or fibrous shapes, stabilized by H-bonds, disulfide linkages (−S−S−), ionic salt bridges, and hydrophobic interactions; 4) Quaternary (4°): Spatial arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits (e.g. Hemoglobin with 4 subunits: 2α + 2β).

Denaturation: Disruption of secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures of a protein by heat, pH change, or chemicals without breaking primary peptide bonds. Protein loses biological activity (e.g. coagulation of egg white on boiling, curdling of milk).

formulas.label: Forces stabilizing tertiary structure
formulas.expr: Hydrogen bonds, Disulfide linkages (−S−S−), Salt bridges (ionic), Hydrophobic van der Waals forces

nodes.title: Nucleic Acids: DNA, RNA & Chargaff's Rules
points: Components of nucleotides: 1) Nitrogenous base: Purines (Adenine 'A', Guanine 'G'); Pyrimidines (Cytosine 'C', Thymine 'T' in DNA, Uracil 'U' in RNA); 2) Pentose sugar: β-D-2-deoxyribose (DNA) vs β-D-ribose (RNA); 3) Phosphate group: Esterified to 5'-OH of sugar.
Nucleoside vs Nucleotide: Nucleoside = Base + Sugar (linked by N-glycosidic bond at C-1'). Nucleotide = Nucleoside + Phosphate (esterified at C-5').
Dinucleotide linkage: Phosphodiester linkage between 3'-OH of one nucleotide sugar and 5'-OH of next. Chain runs 5' → 3'.

DNA Double Helix (Watson and Crick): Two antiparallel polynucleotide chains coiled around central axis. Complementary base pairing via hydrogen bonds: A = T (2 hydrogen bonds); G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds).
Chargaff's Rules: In double-stranded DNA: Moles of Adenine = Moles of Thymine (A = T); Moles of Guanine = Moles of Cytosine (G = C); Total Purines = Total Pyrimidines (A + G = T + C).

formulas.label: Chargaff's Equimolar Rules (double-stranded DNA)
formulas.expr: A = T and G = C; therefore (A + G) / (T + C) = 1

formulas.label: Hydrogen bonds in complementary base pairs
formulas.expr: A = T (2 hydrogen bonds) | G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds)

formulas.label: Nucleotide composition relation
formulas.expr: Nucleotide = Base + Pentose Sugar + Phosphate group (linked at 5' position)

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Reasonings
points: Board Q1: What is Invert sugar and why is it so called? (Explain sucrose inversion from +66.5° to −19.8° due to fructose levorotation).
Board Q2: State proof reactions for: 1) 6 carbon straight chain in glucose; 2) Presence of aldehyde group; 3) 5 hydroxyl groups.
Board Q3: Explain what is meant by Denaturation of proteins and state which structural levels are destroyed (2°, 3°, 4° destroyed; 1° remains intact!).
Board Q4: Define Zwitterion and Isoelectric point with suitable example.
Board Q5: Differences between DNA and RNA: Sugar (2-deoxyribose vs ribose), Bases (Thymine vs Uracil), Structure (Double-stranded helix vs Single strand).

formulas.label: Denaturation impact summary
formulas.expr: Primary structure (peptide sequence) remains intact; 2°, 3°, and 4° structures unfold and lose activity

nodes.title: MHT-CET High-Speed Shortcuts & Calculation Hacks
points: TRAP 1: Optical activity of amino acids: ALL natural amino acids are optically active EXCEPT Glycine (achiral).
TRAP 2: Reducing sugar identification: Sucrose is NON-REDUCING (C-1 of glucose and C-2 of fructose are tied in glycosidic bond). Maltose, Lactose, Glucose, Fructose are REDUCING sugars.
TRAP 3: Starch components: Amylose is water-SOLUBLE and linear (α-1,4). Amylopectin is water-INSOLUBLE and branched (α-1,4 and α-1,6).
TRAP 4: Chargaff's rule calculation: If a DNA sample has 20% Cytosine → G = 20% → G + C = 40% → A + T = 60% → A = 30%, T = 30%!
TRAP 5: Nitrogenous bases: Thymine is 5-methyluracil. Present in DNA, absent in RNA (replaced by Uracil).

formulas.label: Chemical identity of Thymine
formulas.expr: Thymine = 5-Methyluracil (present in DNA; Uracil in RNA)
